findings.declaration: CategoryTheory.Localization.Construction.ψ₁ / ψ₂ (@[simp] on definitions with nolint simpNF)
findings.excerpt:
@[simp]
def ψ₁ {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) : ιPaths W X ⟶ ιPaths W Y := (Paths.of _).map (Sum.inl f)
findings.problem: `ψ₁` and `ψ₂` are `@[simp] def`s, so each generates an unfolding equation `ψ₁ W f = (Paths.of _).map (Sum.inl f)` as a simp lemma. The right-hand side is not in simp normal form, because `Paths.of` is `@[simps]` and its `of_map` lemma rewrites `(Paths.of V).map f` to `f.toPath`. That is the likely cause of the simpNF failure, which the file silences with `attribute [nolint simpNF] ψ₁.eq_1` and `ψ₂.eq_1`. The `#adaptation_note`s admit nobody has diagnosed it. As a result, simp turns the named morphisms of the `relations` constructors and of `Q` into raw `Quiver.Hom.toPath (Sum.inl f)` / `Sum.inr ⟨w, hw⟩` terms. The names `ψ₁`/`ψ₂` then vanish from goals and no longer match the statements of `relations.id`, `comp`, `Winv₁` and `Winv₂`. The file only needs these as notation, since `Q` and `wIso` unfold them by defeq. `wIso` already writes `(Paths.of _).map (Sum.inr ⟨w, hw⟩)` by hand after `dsimp`.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `@[simp]` from `ψ₁` and `ψ₂` and delete the two `attribute [nolint simpNF] ...eq_1` lines and their adaptation notes. This leaves `ψ₁`/`ψ₂` as opaque-to-simp names. If simp-level access is wanted, state one explicit lemma, e.g. `ψ₁ W f = (Sum.inl f).toPath`, whose right-hand side is in normal form, or mark the defs `abbrev`. Callers that need the unfolding can use `dsimp [ψ₁]` explicitly. This could not be compiled here, so the proofs in `Q`, `lift` and `uniq` would need rechecking.
findings.benefit: The simp set no longer contains a lemma whose right-hand side is rewritten again, and the linter workaround and its TODO notes go away. Goals about the path-category relations stay readable and keep matching the `relations` constructors.
